item.title: Unveiling the Global Landscape of Android Security Updates
item.description:
Research overview

This follow-up to our NDSS Android study analyzes 567,000 security-update records from 2014 to 2024, covering 904 devices from six OEMs across 98 countries. We compare update timing across manufacturers, devices, and regions, examine documented vulnerabilities and OEM compliance with Android security guidelines, and identify gaps in patch availability and support. The expanded dataset provides a broader view of Android’s global update ecosystem.

item.title: A Survey on Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
item.description:
Research overview

This survey explains decentralized identifiers and verifiable credentials, their implementations, and their use across digital-identity applications. It covers scenarios beyond individual identity, including cloud, edge, and IoT resources, and reviews relevant initiatives, adoption challenges, and future research directions. It provides background for our EVOKE credential-revocation mechanism, which targets constrained IoT networks.

item.title: Ransomware over Modern Web Browsers: A Novel Strain and a New Defense Mechanism
With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility: Security and Privacy Issues of Modern Browser Application Programming Interfaces
item.description:
Research overview

This article examines the security and privacy consequences of modern browser APIs that expose device capabilities, manage data, and support user interaction. It organizes the API landscape, discusses risks arising from implementation choices and combinations of capabilities, and outlines research directions for improving defenses. The focus is the balance between richer web applications and the larger attack surface they introduce.

item.title: A Comprehensive Security and Performance Assessment of UAV Authentication Schemes
A Review of On-Device Machine Learning for IoT: An Energy Perspective
item.description:
Research overview

This review examines the energy demands of running machine learning close to IoT devices. It organizes research on training and inference, including centralized, distributed, and federated approaches, and discusses the relationship between model performance, resource consumption, privacy, and latency. The survey complements our experimental study of on-device intrusion detection and identifies challenges for energy-efficient deployment.

item.title: Augmenting Security and Privacy in the Virtual Realm: An Analysis of Extended Reality Devices
item.description:
Research overview

This article analyzes security and privacy attacks and defenses from the perspective of extended-reality devices. It examines the risks created by their capabilities and considers how protections can better account for sensitive user information. The analysis develops research directions and design considerations for more secure, privacy-aware XR systems, providing context for our later VR sensor side-channel study.
